passages.title: The Apron with Two Pockets
paragraphs: Grandma gave me an apron（围裙） for our cooking afternoon. One pocket held a small notebook, and the other was empty. I wanted to carry a spoon there, but Grandma said it would be cleaner on a plate. We washed our hands and began making fruit salad. I wrote down the steps whenever we stopped. By lunchtime, my empty pocket held only a folded tissue（纸巾）. My apron had several wet marks, but my shirt was clean. I hung it up after washing it, ready to give Grandma a hand again.

passages.title: A Place for the Wet Boots
paragraphs: After a muddy walk, my brother left his boots beside the door. Small brown marks soon appeared across the floor. I fetched a cloth while he brought an old tray（托盘） from the cupboard. We put the boots on it and wiped the floor together. The tray caught the muddy water as the boots dried. Next morning, we washed it outside and left it by the door. Our new boot station（固定放置处） was simple, but useful. Now we take off our wet boots before walking into the flat.

passages.title: The Button That Matched Nothing
paragraphs: Mum keeps spare buttons in a tin. When a button fell off my cardigan, we searched for another green one. There were round buttons, square buttons and even one shaped like a duck. None was quite right. I chose a yellow button with the same size and number of holes. Mum sewed（缝） it on while I held the tin. My cardigan now looked a little different. At school, a friend noticed the yellow spot and smiled. I liked its cheerful（欢快的） colour and decided to keep it that way.

passages.title: A Menu I Could Read
paragraphs: On holiday, we visited a small restaurant with an English menu. I recognised rice and chicken, but several dishes were new to me. Each had a short description（描述） below its name. One said that the dish contained mushrooms and had a mild taste. I asked the waiter what “mild” meant. He explained that it was not very spicy. That sounded good, so I ordered it. Reading the extra words helped me make a choice. I enjoyed my lunch and added “mild” to my growing food vocabulary（词汇）.

passages.title: The Bookmark with a Window
paragraphs: Sometimes I lost my place while reading a crowded page. My teacher gave me a strip of card with a narrow window（窗口） cut in it. Only one line of words showed through. I moved the card down as I read, and my eyes followed more easily. Later, I made my own from blue card and added a little moon at the top. It also worked as a bookmark. I did not need it for every book, but it helped me concentrate on pages with very small print（印刷字体）.

passages.title: The View beyond Our Classroom
paragraphs: During an art lesson, our teacher asked us to turn our chairs towards the windows. We usually drew things on our desks, but today we would draw the view outside. I noticed a water tank on a roof and three shirts hanging from a balcony（阳台）. My friend drew a delivery rider waiting at the gate. We sat in the same room, yet chose different things. When we held up our pictures, the class window seemed much bigger. Thirty small views had become one lively（生动的） picture of our neighbourhood.

passages.title: The Speech Bubbles in Our Comic
paragraphs: We drew a comic about two children trying to catch a runaway hat. My pictures were ready, but the speech bubbles（气泡框） filled most of the page. I had written everything the children did. My partner pointed out that readers could already see those actions. I shortened the dialogue and let the pictures tell more of the story. Now there was room for the flying hat. We read the comic together, taking turns as the two children. A surprised shout worked better than a long explanation（解释） beneath every picture.

passages.title: The Sentence without a Full Stop
paragraphs: Our teacher wrote a long line on the board without any punctuation. It described a child getting home and feeding a cat, then asked what was inside a mysterious box. We tried reading it aloud, but the actions ran together. I added a full stop after the cat’s dinner. My partner put a question mark at the end. Suddenly, the reader knew where to pause and what to wonder about. The words stayed the same, yet the punctuation（标点） changed how they sounded. We read through the line again with much clearer expression（语气）.

passages.title: The Map We Drew from Memory
paragraphs: Before a school visit, we drew maps of the route from our classroom to the hall without walking there. I remembered the stairs but forgot a courtyard（庭院）. My partner remembered the courtyard but placed the hall on the wrong side. Afterwards, we walked along the route and checked our maps. We added missing corners and crossed out mistakes. I was surprised by the gaps in a journey I made every week. Walking somewhere often did not mean I could keep track of every turn from memory（记忆） alone.

passages.title: The Dictionary Race We Slowed Down
paragraphs: We raced to find words in small English dictionaries. I turned pages quickly but kept passing the word I needed. My partner showed me the guide words at the top of each page. They told us the first and last words on that page. We also checked the second letter when several words began alike. Soon, I was searching more calmly and finding words faster. Knowing the alphabetical（按字母顺序的） order helped me look things up. The race became easier when I understood how the entries（词条） were arranged.

passages.title: The Orange under Its Skin
paragraphs: At breakfast, Dad gave me an orange to examine before eating it. Its skin had tiny dots, and a pale layer lay underneath. I peeled it carefully and pulled apart the segments（瓣）. Each segment contained many small sacs（小囊） filled with juice. I drew what I saw, then ate my orange. Drawing it took longer than simply peeling it, but I noticed much more. The fruit was familiar on the outside and surprisingly detailed inside. Next, I wanted to have a look at the centre of a pear with the same curiosity（好奇心）.

passages.title: The Shadow Puppet with Long Ears
paragraphs: We made shadow puppets using a lamp, a white sheet and our hands. My rabbit had two long ears, but its head looked enormous. I moved my hands farther from the lamp and closer to the sheet. The shadow became smaller. My partner moved her hands the other way, and her bird grew larger. We changed the distance several times, trying to make our animals similar in size. Soon they were ready for a story. Our hands had become characters（角色）, and we could bring them to life behind the screen（幕布）.

passages.title: The Paper Towel Bridge
paragraphs: Our teacher placed a strip of paper towel with one end in coloured water and the other in an empty cup nearby. We watched the wet patch slowly move upwards through the paper. Tiny spaces between its fibres（纤维） allowed water to travel through it. After a while, the water reached the other end and began dripping into the empty cup. We left the cups on a tray and returned later to check them. The paper towel had become a little bridge（桥梁）. We could see for ourselves how the water moved.

passages.title: The Pebble inside the Shoe
paragraphs: Halfway through our walk, I stopped because something hurt my foot. A tiny pebble（小石子） had slipped into my shoe. I shook it out and put the shoe back on. Although the stone was smaller than a pea, walking felt completely different without it. Dad waited while I checked my sock too. We continued towards the park, and I could enjoy the trees again. I had tried ignoring the discomfort for several minutes. Taking a short pause（暂停） to sort it out made the rest of our walk much nicer.

passages.title: A Spider Web without a Spider
paragraphs: Early one morning, we found a spider web stretched between two bushes. Tiny drops of water made its threads shine. I wanted to touch it, but Mum suggested looking closely without disturbing it. Some threads ran outwards from the centre, while others joined them in a spiral（螺旋形）. We could not see the spider. It might be resting nearby, so we left the web alone. As the sun rose, the drops slowly disappeared. I felt lucky to catch sight of such a delicate（精巧的） structure before it became harder to see.

passages.title: The Tree Ring on the Stool
paragraphs: At a craft centre, we sat on stools made from thick slices of tree trunks. I noticed circles on the top of mine. The guide called them growth rings（年轮）. She explained that many trees add a new ring each year as their trunks grow wider. Some rings were broad, while others were narrow. We followed them from the centre towards the bark. The wood held years of growth. Sitting down had given me a chance to learn about the tree’s history（历史） through the patterns in its wood.

passages.title: The Lane beside the Pool Wall
paragraphs: At the swimming pool, ropes divided the water into long lanes. A notice showed which lanes were for lessons and which were for other swimmers. Our instructor led us to the lane beside the wall. We practised short distances while she watched from the side. In the next lane, swimmers moved much faster, but the rope kept our spaces separate. I had seen the bright floats before without thinking about their job. They marked a boundary（分界线） so different groups could share（共用） the pool at the same time.

passages.title: The Theatre Programme
paragraphs: Before a play began, I opened its printed programme（节目单）. It listed the actors, but also people who designed the lights, made the costumes and built the scenery. During the show, a bright room became a dark forest in moments. I wondered who had planned that change. Afterwards, I looked through the names again. The list helped me imagine the work behind the scenes. I could see the actors on stage, but the whole performance depended on a much larger group. I kept the programme as a souvenir（纪念品）.

passages.title: The Last Stop on the Bus
paragraphs: My aunt lives at the last stop of a bus route. When we visited her, I watched the passengers get off until only a few remained. At the final stop, the driver checked that everyone had left before closing the doors. Beside the stop stood a small shelter（候车亭） and a map of the route. I traced our journey with my finger. A line that usually carried me only two stops could take me much farther. Next time, I wanted to explore（探索） another part of it along the way.

passages.title: A Basket Woven from Strips
paragraphs: At a craft workshop, we wove paper strips into small baskets. One strip went over the next, then under another. I forgot the pattern halfway through, leaving a loose gap. The instructor helped me undo（拆开） that part and begin again. Soon, the base held together, and we folded the sides upwards. My basket could carry a few light paper flowers. I ran a finger over its checked pattern. Each strip helped hold the others in place. A flat pile of paper had become a useful little container（容器）.

passages.title: The Mouse and the Tall Stool
paragraphs: A mouse bought a tall stool so she could reach her kitchen shelf. It worked perfectly until her friend the hedgehog came to cook. He found the seat too narrow and the legs rather shaky under his weight. The mouse was surprised because she used it every day. Together, they brought in a lower, wider bench. Both could now reach the bowls comfortably. The mouse kept her stool for her own small corner. Something suitable（合适的） for one person might need an adjustment（调整） when others wanted to make use of it.

passages.title: The Duck Who Collected Questions
paragraphs: A duck carried a notebook full of questions. Why did leaves fall? Where did clouds go? Her friend thought she should stop asking until every page had an answer. The duck disagreed. She left spaces and carried on watching the world. One day, a falling leaf landed beside her notebook. She drew it and added another question about its colour. Her book was still unfinished, but she loved opening it. Some questions needed time. She could look forward to new discoveries（发现） without pretending（假装） to know everything already.

passages.title: The Giant and the Small Door
paragraphs: A giant visited a village library, but its door was too small for him. He could only kneel outside and peer through a window. The librarian wanted him to enjoy the stories too. She brought a chair outside for herself and several books for him. Other readers joined them beneath a tree. Soon, the giant was reading aloud while everyone listened. On sunny days, their outdoor reading group met again. The doorway stayed small, but the welcome grew. A little creativity（创意） helped them make room for an unexpected（意想不到的） guest.

passages.title: The Score We Forgot to Write
paragraphs: My cousin and I played table tennis in the garden. After several exciting rallies, we disagreed about the score. We both felt certain, yet neither had kept a written record. We stopped arguing and agreed to begin a new game. This time, we said the score aloud after every point and moved counters on a small board. The next game went smoothly. We still wanted to win, but we wanted to enjoy playing too. A clear record（记录） helped us avoid（避免） another argument and get on with the game.

passages.title: The Friend Who Needed Some Space
paragraphs: My friend sat quietly during break. I asked if she wanted to join our game, but she shook her head. I nearly asked again because I thought cheering her up was my job. Instead, I said I would be nearby if she wanted company. Later, she came over and told me she was tired after a noisy morning. We sat together for a while before returning to class. I could care about her without asking her to explain immediately. Being a friend also meant respecting her need for peace（安静） and privacy（私人空间）.

passages.title: The Error in My Thank You Note
paragraphs: I wrote a thank you note to my uncle after he helped with my model plane. When I read it again, I noticed that I had written “train” instead of “plane”. I wanted to throw the whole card away, but my sister suggested a neat correction. I crossed out the wrong word once and wrote the right one above it. Then I added a little drawing of the wings. My uncle laughed warmly when he opened it. The correction（修改） did not take away from my gratitude（感激之情）.

passages.title: The First Try on the Other Side
paragraphs: I usually kick a football with my right foot. During practice, our coach asked us to try the left. My first kick hardly moved the ball, and I felt awkward. We stood close to our partners and passed slowly. After several tries, I could send it in roughly the right direction. It still felt strange, but I understood why we were practising. In a game, the ball might arrive on either side. I was getting used to a new movement（动作）, and my weaker foot deserved some practice（练习） too.

passages.title: A Nickname for the Quiz
paragraphs: Our teacher set up an online quiz and asked us to choose nicknames for the screen. I first typed my full name, then wondered whether I needed it. The teacher explained that a simple class nickname was enough. I chose Blue Panda, and my friend became Green Rocket. When the results appeared, everyone laughed at the colourful names. The teacher could still check our work using her class list. I learned to leave out personal details（信息） when they were not needed. My new nickname（昵称） made the quiz more fun too.

passages.title: The Empty Space in Our Picture
paragraphs: Our group painted a large picture of a park. I wanted to fill every corner with flowers and animals. My partner suggested leaving some pale blue space around the pond. At first, I thought it looked unfinished. Then we stepped away and compared it with a crowded sketch. In the larger picture, the pond was easier to notice, and the birds seemed to have room to fly. We put our brushes down. Sometimes, leaving out a detail can improve the whole composition（构图）. Empty space can have a purpose（用途） too.

passages.title: A Skill That Came Back
paragraphs: I found my old yo-yo in a drawer and decided to try it. Years ago, I could make it drop and return smoothly. Now it spun sideways and stayed near the floor. I checked the string（细绳） and tried several slow movements. After a few minutes, one attempt worked. By the end of the afternoon, I could repeat it several times. I was not starting with nothing; some of the old skill remained. It needed a little refreshing（重新温习）. I put the yo-yo where I could pick it up again tomorrow.
